scenes.section_title:
- Primary Learning Objective: Define average acceleration $a_{av} = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$ and instantaneous acceleration $a = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d^2s}{dt^2} = v \frac{dv}{ds}$, understanding how acceleration represents the rate of change of velocity in magnitude and direction.
- Essential Perspectives: Time Limit Progression (\\(\Delta t \to 0\\)), Velocity Rate Perspective ($a = \frac{dv}{dt}$ vs $a = v\frac{dv}{ds}$).
- Supporting Perspectives: Directional Sign Convention ($a > 0 \rightarrow$ acceleration in positive direction, $a < 0 \rightarrow$ deceleration or acceleration in negative direction).
- Evidence Gaps: Excludes physical causes of force or mass (Kinematics boundary).
scenes.generated_prompt:
Time Evolution
Learning Target: Demonstrate that instantaneous acceleration \\(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\\) is the geometric limit of average acceleration \\(a_{av} = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}\\) as time interval \\(\Delta t \to 0\\), and visually prove that opposing velocity and acceleration vectors cause deceleration.

Scene Objects and Initial State:
- Velocity-time curve \\(v(t) = 40 - 5t^2\\) rendered on 2D coordinate canvas (\\(t\\)-axis \\(0\\) to \\(4\text{ s}\\), \\(v\\)-axis \\(0\\) to \\(45\text{ m/s}\\)).
- Initial fixed point \\(A(0, 40\text{ m/s})\\) and secondary point \\(B(2, 20\text{ m/s})\\) with interval \\(\Delta t = 2\text{ s}\\).
- Cyan secant line connecting point \\(A\\) and point \\(B\\).
- Top tracking panel: Particle \\(P\\) moving along horizontal line equipped with green velocity vector arrow \\(\mathbf{v}\\) and red acceleration vector arrow \\(\mathbf{a}\\).

Time Behavior:
- Continuous simulation of limit process \\(\Delta t \rightarrow 0\\).
- Point \\(B\\) slides along \\(v(t)\\) curve toward fixed point \\(A\\) as \\(\Delta t\\) shrinks.
- Play, Pause, and Reset controls govern animation playback.

Custom Perspectives:
- Vector Alignment Perspective: Displays green velocity arrow \\(\mathbf{v}\\) pointing rightwards (\\(+20\text{ m/s}\\)) and red acceleration arrow \\(\mathbf{a}\\) pointing leftwards (\\(-20\text{ m/s}^2\\)), visually reinforcing deceleration.
- Calculus Tangent Limit: Cyan secant line rotates smoothly into orange tangent line at point \\(A\\) as \\(\Delta t \to 0\\).

Governing Rules:
- Average acceleration formula: \\(a_{av} = \frac{v(t_1+\Delta t) - v(t_1)}{\Delta t} = \frac{20 - 40}{2} = -10\text{ m/s}^2\\).
- Instantaneous acceleration derivative: \\(a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = -10t \implies a(2) = -20\text{ m/s}^2\\).
- Differential position relation: \\(a \, ds = v \, dv \implies a = v \frac{dv}{ds}\\).

Learner Investigations and Controls:
- Slider 1: Fixed Time Instant \\(t_1\\) (range \\(0\\) to \\(3\text{ s}\\), default \\(2.0\text{ s}\\)).
- Slider 2: Interval Duration \\(\Delta t\\) (range \\(0.001\text{ s}\\) to \\(2.0\text{ s}\\), default \\(2.0\text{ s}\\)).
- Action: Learner reduces \\(\Delta t\\) slider from \\(2.0\text{ s}\\) to \\(0.001\text{ s} \rightarrow\\) Secant line morphs into tangent line \\(\rightarrow\\) Secant slope display updates from \\(-10\text{ m/s}^2\\) to \\(-20\text{ m/s}^2\\).
- Action: Learner toggles Vector Direction Highlight \\(\rightarrow\\) Particle \\(P\\) displays anti-parallel velocity and acceleration vectors, highlighting speed reduction \\(|v|\\).

Linked Representations:
- Tangent slope on \\(v-t\\) graph directly sets magnitude and orientation of red acceleration arrow \\(\mathbf{a}\\) on the top physical particle track.

Visual Outcome and Misconception Contrast:
- Visually corrects the misconception that negative acceleration always means moving backward, showing that \\(a < 0\\) with \\(v > 0\\) means moving forward while slowing down.

Acceptance Requirements:
- Secant line rotates smoothly into tangent line as \\(\Delta t \rightarrow 0\\).
- Particle \\(P\\) speed \\(|v|\\) visibly decreases when \\(\mathbf{v}\\) and \\(\mathbf{a}\\) vectors point in opposite directions.
- Slope numerical readout accurately reflects derivative \\(-10t\\) at chosen \\(t_1\\).

Limitations:
- Particle mass and forces driving deceleration are omitted (pure kinematics).

first_output.section_identity:
- Primary Learning Objective: Define average acceleration $a_{av} = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$ and instantaneous acceleration $a = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d^2s}{dt^2} = v \frac{dv}{ds}$, understanding how acceleration represents the rate of change of velocity in magnitude and direction.
- Essential Perspectives: Time Limit Progression (\\(\Delta t \to 0\\)), Velocity Rate Perspective ($a = \frac{dv}{dt}$ vs $a = v\frac{dv}{ds}$).
- Supporting Perspectives: Directional Sign Convention ($a > 0 \rightarrow$ acceleration in positive direction, $a < 0 \rightarrow$ deceleration or acceleration in negative direction).
- Evidence Gaps: Excludes physical causes of force or mass (Kinematics boundary).
first_output.core_understanding:
- Baseline Concept: Average acceleration $a_{av} = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{t_2 - t_1}$ measures the average time rate of velocity change. Instantaneous acceleration $a = \frac{dv}{dt}$ is the derivative of velocity with respect to time, which can also be re-expressed by eliminating $dt$ as $a = v \frac{dv}{ds}$.
- Time Perspective:
* Finite Interval (\\(\Delta t = t_2 - t_1\\)): Evaluates total change in velocity \\(\Delta v\\) over duration \\(\Delta t\\).
* Shrinking Interval (\\(\Delta t \to 0\\)): As interval shrinks, average acceleration converges to the exact derivative \\(a(t)\\).
* Time Elimination (\\(a = v \frac{dv}{ds}\\)): Connects velocity, position, and acceleration directly when time \\(t\\) is not explicitly given.
- Custom Perspectives:
* Directional Sign Convention: When \\(v\\) and \\(a\\) have the same sign, speed \\(|v|\\) increases (speeding up). When \\(v\\) and \\(a\\) have opposite signs, speed \\(|v|\\) decreases (slowing down/deceleration).
first_output.visual_first_explanation:

- Limits of Metaphor: Particle is modeled as a point mass without spatial rotation.

- Animation Flow: Learner selects $t_1 = 0\text{ s}$ and drags $\Delta t$ from $2\text{ s}$ down to $0\text{ s}$.
- Interactive Inspection: Readouts display $a_{av} = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{\Delta t} = \frac{20 - 40}{2} = -10\text{ m/s}^2$ updating to instantaneous derivative $a(2) = -10(2) = -20\text{ m/s}^2$ as $\Delta t \to 0$.

first_output.visual_learning_outcome: - The learner will visually observe how the slope of the $v-t$ tangent line defines instantaneous acceleration $a = \frac{dv}{dt}$, and recognize that when velocity and acceleration vectors point in opposite directions, the particle slows down.
first_output.concept_check:
- Activity: Given $v = 40 - 5t^2 \text{ m/s}$, calculate $a_{av}$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 2\text{ s}$, and find $a(2)$.
- Expected Observation: $v(0) = 40\text{ m/s}$, $v(2) = 20\text{ m/s} \rightarrow a_{av} = \frac{20 - 40}{2} = -10\text{ m/s}^2$. Instantaneous acceleration $a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = -10t \rightarrow a(2) = -20\text{ m/s}^2$.
first_output.conceptual_summary: - Average acceleration $a_{av} = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$ is the time-averaged rate of velocity change. Instantaneous acceleration $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = v \frac{dv}{ds}$ is the exact time derivative of velocity, represented geometrically by the tangent slope on a $v-t$ graph.
first_output.colloquial_egyptian_explanation: - العجلة المتوسطة (\\(a_{av}\\)) هي مقدار التغير في السرعة مقسوم على الزمن (\\(\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}\\))، أما العجلة اللحظية (\\(a\\)) فهي معدل تغير السرعة بالنسبة للزمن عند لحظة معينة (\\(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d^2s}{dt^2}\\)). وممكن كمان نلغي الزمن وربط العجلة بالمسافة بالقانون $a = v \frac{dv}{ds}$. هندسياً، العجلة اللحظية هي ميل المماس لمنحنى السرعة والزمن (\\(v-t\\)). ولازم تاخد بالك: لما تكون السرعة والعجلة في نفس الاتجاه الجسم بيسرّع، ولما يكونوا في عكس الاتجاه الجسم بيفرمل (تبطؤ).
first_output.laws_if_any:
- Average Acceleration: $a_{av} = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{t_2 - t_1}$
- Instantaneous Acceleration: $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d^2s}{dt^2}$
- Differential Relationship (Time Eliminated): $a = v \frac{dv}{ds} \iff a \, ds = v \, dv$
first_output.real_life_example:
- لما تدوس على دواسة البنزين في العربية والسرعة تزيد من $40$ كم/س لـ $100$ كم/س في $6$ ثواني، العربية بتكتسب عجلة موجبة في نفس اتجاه الحركة. بس أول ما تدوس فرامل فجأة، العجلة بتبقى بالسالب (عكس اتجاه السرعة) فالسرعة بتقل لحد ما تقف.

scenes.section_title:
- Primary Learning Objective: Analyze rectilinear motion using interrelated position (\\(s-t\\)), velocity (\\(v-t\\)), and acceleration (\\(a-t\\)) graphs via differentiation (slopes) and integration (areas).
- Essential Perspectives: Graphic Differential/Integral Relationship (Slope $s-t \rightarrow v$, Slope $v-t \rightarrow a$; Area under $a-t \rightarrow \Delta v$, Area under $v-t \rightarrow \Delta s$).
- Supporting Perspectives: Sign and Curvature Analysis (Concavity of $s-t$ graph determined by sign of acceleration $a$).
- Evidence Gaps: Non-continuous jump discontinuities in acceleration graphs are treated piecewise.

State Mapping
Learning Target: Prove the triple calculus coupling of rectilinear motion graphs (\\(s-t\\), \\(v-t\\), \\(a-t\\)), establishing that graph slopes perform differentiation (\\(s \to v \to a\\)) while shaded graph areas perform integration (\\(a \to \Delta v \to \Delta s\\)).

Scene Objects and Initial State:
- Triple vertically stacked 2D plot canvases sharing identical time axis \\(t \in [0, 6\text{ s}]\\):
  1. Top Canvas: Position graph \\(x(t) = 6t^2 - t^3\\) (\\(0\\) to \\(35\text{ m}\\)).
  2. Middle Canvas: Velocity graph \\(v(t) = 12t - 3t^2\\) (\\(-36\\) to \\(+15\text{ m/s}\\)).
  3. Bottom Canvas: Acceleration graph \\(a(t) = 12 - 6t\\) (\\(-24\\) to \\(+15\text{ m/s}^2\\)).
- Vertical red time sweep cursor initialized at \\(t_1 = 2.0\text{ s}\\).
- Tangent line indicators attached to curves at cursor intersections.
- Shaded integral area regions under \\(v(t)\\) and \\(a(t)\\) curves from \\(t = 0\\) to \\(t_1\\).

- Dragging time cursor shifts the vertical line continuously, updating tangent slopes and shaded area fills across all three graphs in real time.

Governing Rules:
- Slopes: \\(v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt} = 12t - 3t^2\\), \\(a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = 12 - 6t\\).
- Definite Integrals: \\(\Delta v = \int_{0}^{t_1} (12 - 6t) \, dt\\), \\(\Delta x = \int_{0}^{t_1} (12t - 3t^2) \, dt\\).
- Critical Points: At \\(t = 2\text{ s}\\), \\(v_{max} = 12\text{ m/s}\\) and \\(a = 0\text{ m/s}^2\\). At \\(t = 4\text{ s}\\), \\(x_{max} = 32\text{ m}\\), \\(v = 0\text{ m/s}\\), and \\(a = -12\text{ m/s}^2\\).

- Toggle 2: Tangent Slope Indicators (Displays tangent lines and slope values).

Linked Representations:

Visual Outcome and Misconception Contrast:

first_output.section_identity:
- Primary Learning Objective: Analyze rectilinear motion using interrelated position (\\(s-t\\)), velocity (\\(v-t\\)), and acceleration (\\(a-t\\)) graphs via differentiation (slopes) and integration (areas).
- Essential Perspectives: Graphic Differential/Integral Relationship (Slope $s-t \rightarrow v$, Slope $v-t \rightarrow a$; Area under $a-t \rightarrow \Delta v$, Area under $v-t \rightarrow \Delta s$).
- Supporting Perspectives: Sign and Curvature Analysis (Concavity of $s-t$ graph determined by sign of acceleration $a$).
- Evidence Gaps: Non-continuous jump discontinuities in acceleration graphs are treated piecewise.
first_output.core_understanding:
- Baseline Concept: Kinematic graphs form a calculus-linked chain. The slope of $s-t$ graph gives $v(t)$; the slope of $v-t$ graph gives $a(t)$. Conversely, the definite area under $a-t$ graph over interval $\Delta t$ equals change in velocity $\Delta v$, and the definite area under $v-t$ graph equals displacement $\Delta s$.
- Time Perspective:
* Forward Differentiation (Time Derivative Progression): \\(s(t) \xrightarrow{\text{slope}} v(t) \xrightarrow{\text{slope}} a(t)\\).
* Backward Integration (Time Accumulation Progression): \\(a(t) \xrightarrow{\text{area}} \Delta v \xrightarrow{\text{area}} \Delta s\\).
* Concavity & Time Turning Points: Zero slope on \\(s-t \implies v = 0\\) (turning point); inflection point on \\(s-t \implies a = 0\\).
- Custom Perspectives:
* Concavity Perspective: Positive acceleration (\\(a > 0\\)) corresponds to concave up position curve (\\(s-t\\)). Negative acceleration (\\(a < 0\\)) corresponds to concave down position curve (\\(s-t\\)).
first_output.visual_first_explanation:
- Triple Synchronized Stacked Canvas: Top panel $s-t$ curve (\\(x = 6t^2 - t^3\\)), middle panel $v-t$ curve (\\(v = 12t - 3t^2\\)), bottom panel $a-t$ line (\\(a = 12 - 6t\\)).
- Vertical Time Sweep Line: A vertical cursor at $t_1$ traverses all three graphs simultaneously, highlighting slopes and accumulating areas.
- Limits of Metaphor: Graphs represent continuous mathematical functions without mechanical noise or measurement error.
first_output.visual_scene_script:
- Scene Setup: Function $x(t) = 6t^2 - t^3$ displayed across 3 vertically aligned plot canvases for $t \in [0, 6\text{ s}]$.
- Animation Flow: Learner drags time marker $t$ from $0$ to $6\text{ s}$.
- Interactive Inspection:
* At \\(t = 2\text{ s}\\): \\(x = 16\text{ m}\\), slope on \\(s-t\\) equals \\(12\text{ m/s}\\) (\\(v=12\\)), slope on \\(v-t\\) equals \\(0\text{ m/s}^2\\) (\\(a=0\\), local peak of \\(v-t\\)).
* At \\(t = 4\text{ s}\\): \\(x = 32\text{ m}\\) (local peak of \\(s-t\\)), slope on \\(s-t\\) equals \\(0\text{ m/s}\\) (\\(v=0\\)), \\(a = -12\text{ m/s}^2\\) (decelerating).
first_output.dynamic_view_blueprint:
- Visible Objects: Stacked $s-t$, $v-t$, and $a-t$ plot axes, vertical synchronized time indicator line, slope tangent indicators, area fill shaded regions under $v-t$ and $a-t$.
- Interactions:
* Move time slider \\(t \rightarrow\\) vertical line sweeps all 3 graphs simultaneously \\(\rightarrow\\) live displays of tangent slopes on top graph matching y-values on graph below it.
* Toggle Area Shading \\(\rightarrow\\) shades area under \\(v-t\\) from \\(t_1\\) to \\(t_2 \rightarrow\\) readout demonstrates Area \\(= \int v \, dt = \Delta s\\).
first_output.visual_learning_outcome: - Learner will visually verify that the y-coordinate of the $v-t$ graph matches the slope of the $s-t$ graph at every instant, and the shaded area under the $v-t$ curve equals the net height difference $\Delta s$ on the $s-t$ graph.
first_output.concept_check:
- Activity: For position function $x = 6t^2 - t^3$, determine position, velocity, and acceleration at $t = 2\text{ s}$ and $t = 4\text{ s}$.
- Expected Observation: At $t = 2\text{ s}$: $x = 16\text{ m}$, \\(v = 12\text{ m/s}\\), \\(a = 0\text{ m/s}^2\\). At \\(t = 4\text{ s}\\): \\(x = 32\text{ m}\\) (max height), \\(v = 0\text{ m/s}\\), \\(a = -12\text{ m/s}^2\\).
first_output.conceptual_summary: - Kinematic graphs are mathematically coupled: slopes move downward through differentiation (\\(s \to v \to a\\)), while areas move upward through integration (\\(a \to \Delta v \to \Delta s\\)).
first_output.colloquial_egyptian_explanation: - منحنيات الحركة (\\(s-t, v-t, a-t\\)) متوصلين ببعض بالتفاضل والتكامل! لو معاك منحنى الموضع \\(s-t\\)، ميل المماس بتاعه يديك منحنى السرعة \\(v-t\\). وميل مماس منحنى السرعة \\(v-t\\) يديك منحنى العجلة \\(a-t\\). والعكس بالعكس: المساحة تحت منحنى العجلة \\(a-t\\) بتديك التغير في السرعة \\(\Delta v\\)، والمساحة تحت منحنى السرعة \\(v-t\\) بتديك الإزاحة \\(\Delta s\\).
first_output.laws_if_any:
- Differentiation (Slopes): \\(v(t) = \frac{ds}{dt} = \text{Slope of } s-t\\), \\(a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = \text{Slope of } v-t\\)
- Integration (Areas): \\(\Delta v = v_2 - v_1 = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} a \, dt = \text{Area under } a-t\\), \\(\Delta s = s_2 - s_1 = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} v \, dt = \text{Area under } v-t\\)
